text.text: Handwriting, hurried: "Took the car.  Went to your mother's.  If you get this, we went to your mother's."
A shopping list.  Bread, milk, batteries, batteries, batteries, batteries.
"I am not going to the shelter.  I know what you think about that.  I love you.  Don't come looking."
A note beginning "By the time you read this" and stopping after four words.
Directions to somewhere, in someone else's handwriting, with a small map on the back.
"Feed the cat.  I mean it.  Feed the cat."
A phone number, written large, gone over so many times the paper has torn.
"Everyone says it will be over by the weekend.  I am writing this down so I can see how stupid it looks."
A child's handwriting: "dear mum i am fine at nans dont worry"
An apology, unaddressed, to somebody the writer clearly expected to see again.
A page torn from a diary.  The entry is about a bad day at work, three days before the Cataclysm.
"If you are reading this you got in.  There is nothing left in here.  Sorry.  Try the house opposite."

text.text: A printed rota for the week of the Cataclysm.  Someone has drawn a small cheerful sun next to Friday.
A resignation letter, typed, signed, and never handed in.
A login and password on a sticky note, which is exactly where the training said not to put it.
Minutes of a meeting about quarterly targets.  The last line is "any other business - none".
An expense claim for a taxi, with a receipt still stapled to it.
A memo reminding staff that the emergency exits are not to be used as smoking areas.
A leaving card for someone called Denise, signed by eleven people.
A performance review scheduled for a date that never happened.
A printed email: "As discussed, please work from home until further notice.  This is precautionary."
A desk calendar page.  Every day that week has been crossed off in advance.
A note to a colleague: "Covered your shift.  You owe me.  Twice now."

text.text: Triage notes.  The list of names runs down the page and continues on the back.
A handover sheet for a shift that was never handed over.
A prescription, written out and never collected.
Observations taken every fifteen minutes, then every five, then not at all.
A printed protocol for an infection, with three lines crossed out and "NO" written beside them.
A page of dosages in careful handwriting, the last entry finished by somebody else.
A ward list.  Most names have a small tick.  Four do not.
A note clipped to nothing: "tell the family before they hear it elsewhere".
An order for supplies, marked URGENT, dated the day everything stopped.
A scrap reading only "bay 4 - do not open" in three different pens.

text.text: Two people on a beach, squinting.  Someone has written a date on the back and then crossed it out.
A dog in a garden, mid-leap, slightly out of focus.
A wedding photograph, folded down the middle so that only one person is showing.
A group of colleagues at a Christmas party, wearing paper hats without enthusiasm.
A child on a bicycle with stabilisers, being held upright by an arm out of frame.
A house with a sold sign outside it, and two people standing very deliberately in front of the sign.
A blurred photograph of a birthday cake.  The candles say 40.
A passport photo strip, four frames.  In the last one, they are laughing.
An old holiday snapshot of somewhere hot.  On the back: "we should go back".
A photograph of a photograph, taken badly, as though the original could not be taken away.
